headline: Nvidia has taken minority stakes in four French start-ups, including the medical appointments platform Doctolib and the robotics AI company Genesis AI.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a large chip maker backing four start-ups across health, robotics, software and materials, announced by Nvidia itself, though amounts are unknown.
importance_line: Four French start-ups in health, robotics, software and materials gain a large backer, but no amounts were disclosed, and critics argue that Nvidia's investments are circular because the money can return to Nvidia as chip purchases, which Huang rejects.
summary: Trending Topics reports, citing Nvidia's blog post and Les Echos, that the chip maker has invested in Doctolib, a medical appointment platform that is building AI agents for doctors; Genesis AI, a robotics start-up developing AI models for general-purpose robots; Pigment, a Paris business-planning software company; and Entalpic, which uses AI to design new materials, with Les Echos describing all four as minority stakes and neither side disclosing amounts. Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang announced the deals in Paris on a European tour, saying "Europe needs to get in the race", and Trending Topics adds that Nvidia plans another $2 billion of European deals within a week, citing The Next Web.
notes: Reuters original (pool link) blocked with HTTP 401; text read at Trending Topics, which relays Nvidia's blog post and Les Echos. Reuters, Les Echos (via Yahoo Finance) and France 24 carried the same news.
